Warehouse operations handbook, section four: receiving and put-away.

Every inbound pallet is checked against its advance shipping notice before it leaves the dock.​ The receiving clerk scans the pallet label, confirms the carton count against the notice, and records any discrepancy on the same screen.​ A discrepancy of one carton or fewer is logged and the pallet proceeds; anything larger holds the pallet in the quarantine lane until a supervisor has signed it off.

Put-away follows the location rules held in the warehouse management system.​ Fast-moving stock is assigned to the lower two levels of the racking nearest the pick faces, and slow-moving stock goes to the upper levels. The system proposes a location when the pallet is scanned; the operator may override it, and an override is recorded with the operator's identifier and a reason code. Overrides are reviewed weekly, and a location that is overridden more than three times in a month is flagged for a rules change rather than left to be worked around.

Temperature-controlled stock is handled separately. Chilled goods move from the dock to the chill room within twenty minutes of the trailer doors opening, and the clock starts when the seal is broken rather than when the first pallet is moved. A temperature excursion is recorded against the consignment, not against the pallet, because a single trailer load can be split across several put-away runs and the excursion applies to all of them.

Damaged stock never enters the racking. It is moved to the damages bay, photographed, and booked against the supplier's account within the same shift. Photographs are attached to the goods receipt so that a claim can be raised without a second inspection. Stock that is damaged in the warehouse rather than in transit is booked against the internal damages code, and the two are never merged, because the supplier claim process depends on the distinction.

Cycle counting runs continuously rather than as an annual stock take. Every location is counted at least twice a year, fast-moving locations every six weeks, and any location with a negative on-hand balance is counted the same day. A count that differs from the system balance by more than two units is recounted by a second operator before the adjustment is posted, and the adjustment carries both operators' identifiers.

Questions about this section go to the warehouse manager. The handbook is reviewed every six months and the review date is recorded on the cover sheet.
